detail:
The National MS Society describes the Pathways to Cures roadmap as the framework organizing MS research worldwide. The roadmap was built through global consensus, with input from scientists, clinicians, funders, and people living with MS, and is endorsed by MS organizations around the world. It groups the search for cures into three pathways that span the course of the disease.

Under the Stop pathway, the goal is no new disease activity and no new symptoms. The Restore pathway focuses on repairing damage to the central nervous system and restoring lost abilities. The End pathway aims to prevent MS in the first place, so there are no new diagnoses. The Society funds research projects across many countries that map onto these pathways, and frames the three together as what a cure for MS would have to accomplish.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about multiple sclerosis research directions.
sourceVideoTitle: Pathways to a Cure for MS
summary: The National MS Society describes its Pathways to Cures roadmap, a global research framework organized around three goals: stopping MS, restoring function through repair, and ending MS through prevention.
takeaways: the pathways to cures roadmap organizes research into stop, restore, and end
stop means no new disease activity and no new symptoms
restore focuses on repairing damage and regaining lost abilities
research participation is optional; talk to your doctor about studies
title: Where multiple sclerosis research is heading
